title: Coordinate and fraction data for permissible standard-basis corrections
statement: Let $T$ be a commutative ring, $r,s\ge0$, $x=(x_0,\ldots,x_r)$, $y=(y_1,\ldots,y_s)$, $P=(x_0,\ldots,x_r)$ and $\mathfrak b$ an ideal. Reuse the coordinate quotient $D=T[t_i\mid1\le i\le r]/(x_i-x_0t_i)$, with its labelled ratio classes, of [def-trf-permissible-coordinate-chart-ring], and the chart subalgebra $C=(T/\mathfrak b)[\bar P/\bar x_0]\subset(T/\mathfrak b)[1/\bar x_0]$ [def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring]. The ambient coordinate map $\iota:D\to T[1/x_0]$ is specified by $h\mapsto h/1$ on $T$ and $t_i\mapsto x_i/x_0$; the quotient coordinate map $\rho:D\to C$ is specified by $h\mapsto\bar h/1$ and $t_i\mapsto\bar x_i/\bar x_0$. These generator identities define the corresponding map predicates. For a prime $z$ of $C$ let $p'=\rho^{-1}(z)$, $T'=D_{p'}$ and $\mathfrak b'=\ker(T'\to C_z)$, where the map is the canonical localized ring map [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Let $\lambda:T\to T'$ be the composite structural map and $H=(x_0,y_1,\ldots,y_s)T'$. An element $g\in T'$ is the divided image of $f\in T$ by $x_0^e$ when there exists $h\in D$ with $\iota(h)=f/x_0^e$ in $T[1/x_0]$ and $h/1=g$ in $T'$. For local $T$, let $k=T/\mathfrak M$ [def-weil-residue-field]. The residue polynomial map $T[t]\to k[t]$ reduces coefficients and preserves ratio labels. For a prime $p$ of $k[t]$, let $L=k[t]_p$, $N$ its maximal ideal and $U_d=\{\phi\in k[X_0,\ldots,X_r]_d:\phi(1,t)/1\in N^d\}$; all polynomials use [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. A parameter graded map $\chi:k[X,Y]\to\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak M}T$ is specified by the canonical degree-zero inclusion on $k$ and the degree-one classes of $x_i,y_j$ [def-trf-local-standard-basis-invariants], with the degree-one classes given by the initial-form inclusion of [def-sfb-nodal-tangent-comparison-data]. For any finite family $(g_i)_{i<m}$ and $a<m$, define $J_a=(g_j:j<a)$ and, for coefficients $c_j$ in the same commutative ring, $g_a^*=g_a-\sum_{j<a}c_jg_j$. Empty prefixes use the zero ideal and zero sum. This defines rings, maps specified on generators, and predicates only; it asserts no existence, injectivity, regularity or correction theorem.

from.place: Historical nearby-duality/alteration branch of lem-trf-local-term-locality, proof (1)--(2), through lem-trf-log-regular-desingularization: monoidal resolution used for the regular modification of nodal pairs; ILO VIII 3.3.15, pp.109--110. Expose VIII, Theorems 3.1.27 and 3.2.20, and Remark 3.2.21, pp.102,106; construction in 3.2.19 over k=Q. Supporting source: Expose VIII, Theorem 2.3.10, normalized restriction in 2.3.9 and Remark 2.3.12(i), equivariance in Corollary 2.3.17, printed pp.93--95; application in 3.2.19, p.106. Refinement in this split: Expose VIII, Theorem 2.3.10 restricted to finite-type Q-schemes, with tower conventions 2.1.4, 2.3.1, 2.3.4 and Remark 2.3.5(i), printed pp.87,91--93. This is ordinary resolution, not the normalized toric conclusion; no Stacks tag states this characteristic-zero resolution theorem. Lower input: embedded characteristic-zero resolution and invariant synchronization discussed in ILO VIII 2.3.11 and 2.3.13; the intrinsic gluing argument is supplied in this item. Lower input: Expose VIII 2.3.11 and 2.3.13, pp.93--94: local invariant input underlying the cited strong embedded algorithm; BMT sections 6.1--6.3, especially local embedding independence and the correction of synchronization for arbitrary smooth morphisms. Lower input: Smooth-stable Hilbert--Samuel head and component-dimension correction. Refinement here: Component-dimension rigidity at a Hilbert--Samuel near point of a blowup. Supporting refinement: Normal-flat normal cone and linear vertex at a Hilbert--Samuel near point. Lower input here: Theorem 2.10(2), printed pp.32--33, and the characteristic-independent additive-subgroup argument in the proof of Theorem 2.14, printed p.36, before its linearity argument: Hironaka [H4], Certain numerical characters of singularities, Theorem IV, and [H5], Additive groups associated with points of a projective space, Theorem 2. The normal-cone quotient used there is Theorem 2.2(2)(ii), printed p.28. Refinement in Q87: Numerical near-point input: normal-cone equations have generators in the projective-point order algebra. Q103 refinement: Proposition 21(i),(ii), p.181, using the order algebra of section 13, p.168, and the chart convention on p.169; the case of equal degree sequences satisfies its non-strict lexicographic hypothesis. The proposition follows from Lemma 20, pp.175–181; Q63 refinement: the inductive correction of a single index in Hironaka Lemma 20, pp.176–181, used to assemble Proposition 21, p.181. Coordinate definitions for Hironaka Lemma 20.
